working_title: Keeping local history alive in different ways

exercise.instructions: You are going to read four profiles of people who are involved in preserving local history. For questions 43–52, choose from the profiles A–D. The profiles may be chosen more than once.
exercise.matching_intro: Read the profiles and answer the questions that follow.
exercise.common_context_title: Different Ways to Preserve Local History

A.label: A
A.text: I started volunteering for an oral history project after listening to my elderly neighbour's fascinating stories. It struck me how many personal memories are never recorded. My role involves interviewing older residents and recording their conversations. While I enjoy capturing these personal experiences, a challenge I face is when interviewees drift into memories that are hard to verify. I've learnt to ask open questions and cross-check basic facts where possible. I now value ordinary memories more than famous events, but I’ve become more cautious about separating memory from fact.

B.label: B
B.text: When I saw our local community cinema closed and neglected, I felt compelled to help restore it. I joined a group of volunteers aiming to bring it back to life. The work is less glamorous than I expected, involving a lot of cleaning and repairing. However, I enjoy the teamwork and learning that some changes are necessary for modern use. While I initially had romantic notions about restoration, I now accept compromises if it means the building can function again.

C.label: C
C.text: I discovered boxes of old family and street photographs that were unidentified. This inspired me to create a digital photo archive to make these images searchable and accessible. A difficulty I encounter is that many photos lack dates or names, and online descriptions can easily become guesses. I invite local residents to help identify people and places, ensuring any uncertain information is clearly labelled. I find it most satisfying when several small clues come together to identify an image.

D.label: D
D.text: I organise local walking tours because friends often asked about the unusual buildings in our neighbourhood. I aim to help residents notice the places they pass every day. The main challenge is keeping the tours engaging without turning uncertain stories into facts. I build routes around visible details and adjust the pace according to the group. While I believe curiosity is important, I’ve learnt that trust matters more, so I leave out stories that cannot be supported.
